q1_open_feedback: We need transparent algorithmic audits before deploying automated voting mechanisms.
Prioritize human moderation oversight over pure LLM summary aggregation.
Decentralized preference elicitation provides better minority protection than single-winner rules.
Ensure verifiable cryptographic provenance for all participant submissions and weights.
Quadratic utility scoring should be used to gauge intensity of preferences.
Consensus thresholds must prevent tyranny of the majority in sensitive policy domains.
Fast iterative feedback loops are vital, but never sacrifice auditability for speed.
Participant identity privacy must be guaranteed while preserving non-repudiation.
Multi-stakeholder review boards should review edge cases where Condorcet cycles occur.
Empirical sensitivity bounds should accompany every collective choice result.
